Title: Community Amenity Contributions Policy Update
Note: Vote on the main Motion, as amended. The text shown is the motion as first moved; it was amended before this vote. See the minutes for the final wording.
Motion text: Be it resolved that Council hereby directs staff to prepare an update to Community Amenity Contributions Council Policy 07-166 for Council’s consideration, no later than the December 12, 2022 Regular Council Meeting, as follows: A. Add a new Climate Action Fund related to mitigating environmental impacts originating from development upon the Township of Langley for items within its Climate Action Strategy related to corporate buildings, habitat preservation and agricultural areas; B. Update the prescribed percentages of available contributions per category as applicable and appropriate to achieve the proposed changes itemized herein and for a wider range of possible use of the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund; C. Consider inclusion of amenity contributions proportionate to the value being created for exceptional land use changes, such as the conversion of agricultural or rural land to industrial or more intensive urban uses; D. Implement an individual community or distinct area-based approach per residential unit type as appropriate; E. Ensure improved regional parity and competitiveness with a provision for additional density per square metre for higher density development forms; and F. Update and/or revise for the provision of an increased array of needed community amenities: a. A new indoor pool and community centre within Yorkson Community Park in Willoughby; P. OTHER BUSINESS b. A new soccer campus within the Smith Neighbourhood Plan in Willoughby; c. A new ice and dry floor recreation facility at the Langley Events Centre in Willoughby; d. Additional high-quality urban parks in urban areas; e. New Fire Hall(s) as may be required for improved service for north Willoughby and Brookswood-Fernridge; and f. A revised inclusion or removal of “Township-wide Greenway” and/or “Satellite RCMP Detachment”.

Title: Final Resolution of North Langley Water Issues
Motion text: Whereas: 1. Numerous concerns over many years have been expressed by the community about the chronically low pH levels of the groundwater- based Township of Langley potable water supply system within areas of North Langley and within Fort Langley, especially, and as it may also affect overall water quality; 2. The water supply and distribution system with Metro Vancouver for North Langley has sufficient capacity to supply additional quantities of potable water to Walnut Grove and Fort Langley from the Coquitlam Reservoir; and 3. Metro Vancouver has resolved pH concerns with the reliable provision of water above and beyond the required standards for pH with an ongoing target of 8.3-8.5 specifically maintained to protect against possible corrosion; Therefore be it resolved that Council hereby directs staff to: A. Decommission Fort Langley Well #2 and cease the extraction of ground water at this location as soon as possible with replacement potable water supply provided by additional bulk water purchases from Metro Vancouver; B. Immediately cease all ongoing activities to expand or otherwise improve Fort Langley Well #2 to otherwise attempt to address pH or water quality issues within previously approved budget envelopes for this purpose; C. Outline the potential demolition, removal, restoration and/or disposition of Fort Langley Well #2 for Council’s consideration within the 2023 budget process; and D. Prepare an updated Report to Council with a potential timeline, cost(s) and capital and operating savings to cease all ongoing Township of P. OTHER BUSINESS Langley water treatment capital projects and extraction and treatment of ground water throughout the Township of Langley, where possible, potentially replaced by additional bulk water purchases from Metro Vancouver, for Council’s consideration within the 2023 budget process.

Title: 40 Additional Suppression Firefighters 2023-2026
Motion text: Whereas: 1. The Township of Langley has experienced considerable growth in population and that this growth is expected to continue for the foreseeable future; 2. This additional population growth necessitates additional public safety infrastructure and staffing resources to adequately serve the community now and in the future; and 3. Public safety is a top priority for The Township of Langley Council; Therefore be it resolved that Council direct staff to provide options within the 2023-2027 Five Year Financial Plan that will result in a complement increase of 40 career suppression firefighters within the next four annual budgets.

Title: Deference to Federal and Provincial Regulations on Single-Use Items
Motion text: Whereas: 1. On May 30, 2022, Council directed staff to prepare a report to Council on the implementation of a Township of Langley bylaw to restrict single- use items; and 2. The federal government has passed legislation to eliminate single-use plastic items, while the provincial government has published an intentions paper that will harmonize how single-use items will be regulated in BC, regardless of the material they are made from; Therefore be it resolved that Council hereby directs staff to not proceed further on the development of Township of Langley bylaw(s) and any preparations for bylaw enforcement thereof or budget requests related thereto.

Title: 10 Additional Bylaw Enforcement Officers 2023-2026
Motion text: Whereas: P. OTHER BUSINESS 1. Improving public safety in all areas is a top priority clearly communicated and previously supported by the majority of Township of Langley Council within this Council term; 2. The Township of Langley has and is experiencing significant residential and commercial growth rates while not having substantially increased its bylaw enforcement capacity for many years; and 3. More bylaw enforcement capacity will assist and provide for an improved level of service and the possibility for Council to consider a more proactive bylaw enforcement policy within our rural areas, especially; Therefore be it resolved that Council direct staff to include within the 2023-2027 Five Year Financial Plan, 10 additional Bylaw Enforcement Officers with 3 added within 2023, 3 in 2024 and 2 in 2025 and 2026, respectively, all with effective start dates of July 1st, respectively.

Title: Obsolescence of GHG Emissions Reduction DPAs
Topics: Housing & density; Environment & climate; Business & economy
Motion text: Whereas: 1. Current requirements for multiple application and permit types negatively affects processing timelines for residential and commercial developments while delaying the provision of housing, economic development and transportation infrastructure; and 2. The Township of Langley’s Building Bylaw includes Energy Step Code requirements for residential buildings, with additional Provincial regulations for non-residential buildings expected; Therefore be it resolved that Council hereby directs staff to prepare a report to Council with the necessary amendments to the applicable bylaws to eliminate the Energy Conservation and GHG Emissions Reduction Development Permit Area(s) and related application requirements.

Title: Mobile Integrated Crisis Response Teams
Motion text: Whereas: 1. Mobile Integrated Crisis Response (MICR) Teams (also known as Car 67) provide expert support to people in crisis and free up police resources to focus on crime; 2. The Province is expanding MICR Teams to nine communities across the province, including municipalities in the region such as Abbotsford, Port Coquitlam/Coquitlam, Burnaby, and Chilliwack; and 3. The Township of Langley was not included in the list of communities identified in the provincial MICR Teams expansion as part of the Province’s Safer Communities Action Plan; Therefore be it resolved that Council hereby directs staff to request the following information from the Langley RCMP and report to Council on: A. Existing mental health services offered by the Langley RCMP; B. The plan for Mobile Integrated Crisis Response (MICR) and associated costs; and C. Data analysis including: a. the number and percentage share of police calls for service that are mental health related for the last 10 years (year over year) and comparators to other lower mainland RCMP and municipal detachments; and Q. OTHER BUSINESS b. a comparison of the percentage of calls for service mental health related to the municipalities prioritized in the MICR provincial announcement.

Title: Drug Use in Public Spaces
Motion text: Whereas: 1. In response to concerns from residents, the Province of British Columbia will now prohibit the possession and use of decriminalized drugs within 15 metres of any play structure in a playground, spray park, wading pool or skateboard park, effective September 18, 2023; 2. Revised prohibitions on possession and use are not comprehensive and do not restrict the possession or use of decriminalized drugs on community sports fields, for example, while prohibiting them at schools, for example; and 3. Residents deserve to feel safe in their own communities and have confidence that public safety hazards and concerns can be resolved; Therefore be it resolved that Council hereby directs staff to report to Council with the necessary amendments to Public Spaces Regulation Bylaw 2018 No. 5298 to prohibit the possession or use of decriminalized drugs in public spaces, including parks.

Title: Voluntary Water Metering Program for Residential Areas
Motion text: Whereas: 1. Multiple municipalities within the region, such as the City of Richmond and the City of Delta, have completed or have ongoing voluntary residential water metering programs where the municipality installs a water meter for a single-family home at no cost to the property owner, wherein the property owner can transition to water metering or continue to pay a flat fee within the water utility as they do now; 2. Water metering offers residents equitable billing to only pay for the water they use, potentially reducing living costs for those that wish to reduce water consumption but would not otherwise realize cost savings; and 3. Water metering on a wider scale of implementation encourages the conservation of water resources and is an effective detection system for leaks and water loss, further reducing costs and reducing water consumption when these leaks are promptly repaired; Therefore be it resolved that Council directs staff to report to Council with: A. A summary of current water metering bylaw(s) and/or policies, billing processes and the percentage of water metering implemented throughout the Township of Langley for non- residential, mixed-used, multi-family, multiple dwelling unit and single family properties where water metering may or may not be mandatory and/or required for new construction; B. An outline of a potential, new multi-year voluntary program to start within the 1st quarter of 2025 for existing single family residential and/or other urban property type owners or strata corporations within the water utility (excluding any and all agricultural properties) without water metering to request the installation of a water meter at no cost for Council to consider no later than the 2nd quarter of 2024, informed by the 2019 Metro Vancouver Best Practices Guide for Local Governments for Residential Water Metering; C. Capital and operating cost implications to the water utility with options including any needed additional staff resources, equipment, implementation and ongoing maintenance, potentially funded by Capital Works within the Water Utility specific to a voluntary water metering program, if so endorsed by Council; D. Potential inclusion of a website portal similar in concept to the City of Abbotsford, such that residents can view their water usage information with methods and options to reduce water usage and to see usage levels in comparison to other properties throughout the Township of Langley of the same property type; E. Consideration of a transition to quarterly or monthly billing for water utility users with water metering; and F. Consideration of a process and cost for pubic input and consultation and/or an open house(s) on a potential voluntary residential water metering program, if so endorsed by Council, R. OTHER BUSINESS with sample quality promotional and educational materials for Council’s consideration.

Note: Vote on the main Motion.
Motion text: Whereas: 1. Bill 44 Housing Statutes (Residential Development) Amendment Act, 2023 (“Bill 44”) will require that all municipalities within the Province of British Columbia grant, by right, up to 4-6 dwelling units per any existing single family lot greater than 280 m2 and less than 4,050 m2; 2. Bill 44 mandates that off-street parking cannot be required for dwelling units required to be granted, such that Council cannot require “off-street parking or loading spaces for the residential use of a housing unit required to be permitted” (14 Section 525); 3. Bill 44 and its provisions would be applicable to any newly created single family areas once created, arbitrarily, by right, increasing dwelling unit densities without off-street parking or other provisions applicable to single family designations within the Township of Langley, including those with secondary suites; and 4. Due to Bill 44, the recently adopted Booth, Rinn, Fernridge Neighbourhood Plans contemplated of 47,000 residents is now projected to be approximately 115,000 to 120,000 residents (not including Glenwood) without any necessary neighbourhood planning for school sites, park capacity, recreation facilities and engineering services plans; Therefore be it resolved that Council hereby directs staff to initiate the repeal of the Booth, Rinn and Fernridge Neighbourhood Plans as soon as it is confirmed that the Township of Langley has not been granted an exemption from the implementation of Bill 44 2023 Housing Statutes (Residential Development) Amendment Act via legislation or regulations for developing areas within the Urban Containment Boundary. Title: Tree Protection Bylaw Permit Fees
Topics: Taxes & spending; Environment & climate; Business & economy; Governance & elections
Motion text: Whereas: P. OTHER BUSINESS 1. Council has recently received multiple Delegations to Council requesting that it (re)consider the high cost of current permit fees and cash-in-lieu charges, especially on relatively small residential construction projects, such as additions, improvements or accessory buildings; and 2. In some cases, the current Fees and Charges required for a relatively small construction project could be considered an unintended consequence that Council should (re)consider, as requested by Delegates to Council, and others within the community; Therefore be it resolved that Council hereby directs staff to bring forward draft bylaw amendments to the Tree Protection Bylaw 2019 No 5478 and Fees and Charges Bylaw 2022 No 5841 that: 1. simplifies the cash-in-lieu provision of 2-1 for trees greater than 30cm dbh within Section 9.1 to instead reside within fees and charges with improved clarity, equity and consistency, as it may be appropriate for Council to consider; 2. simplifies the currently duplicated per-tree permit fees replacing them with a single pro-rated permit fee set at 5% of the total Cash-In-Lieu Fee for Removed Trees (Per Tree), or a minimum of $100, whichever is greater; 3. increases the current fee for Trees Removed Without a Permit to $2,500 per tree; and 4. presents other options that may improve permit processing timelines, tree protection, and equability as it may be appropriate for Council to consider.

Title: Emergency Shelter and Warming Centres
Note: Vote on the main Motion, as amended. The text shown is the motion as first moved; it was amended before this vote. See the minutes for the final wording.
Motion text: Whereas extreme weather events exacerbate the challenges for people experiencing homelessness; Whereas in the past the Township of Langley has partnered with local churches and non-profit organizations to support those in need of shelter during extreme weather events but currently have no such partnerships; Whereas the Township of Langley continues to provide funding to the Gateway of Hope to support their ongoing operations, emergency shelter and warming centre; Whereas the Township of Langley is seeing more people experiencing homelessness and according to the Township of Langley’s Housing Action Plan 2020 homelessness has more than doubled in the past decade; P. OTHER BUSINESS Whereas there is a growing need for emergency shelters in the Township of Langley especially in the outlying areas like Walnut Grove and Aldergrove; and Whereas there are costs related to potential damages, cleaning, staffing and security associated with the operation of an emergency warming shelter; Therefore be it resolved that staff explore potential options to partner with or support local non-profit and or faith based organizations in operating an emergency shelter in the Township of Langley with Aldergrove as a potential first priority; and further Be it resolved that staff explore potential options, provincial grants and or corporate funding to support initiatives related to emergency and warming centres.

Title: Additional Development Phasing Within Willoughby
Motion text: Whereas: O. OTHER BUSINESS 1. The Township of Langley’s population is expected to double by 2050 to over 300,000 residents, with approximately 2,800 acres of undeveloped, urban land that is designated to accommodate up to 50,000 more homes; 2. Recently approved Provincial Housing Statutes, otherwise known as “Bill 44, 46 and 47,” necessitate the possible provision of even more housing within established areas, such as Walnut Grove and Murrayville, with likely unintended financial and infrastructure implications still to be determined; 3. Many areas within Willoughby have detention, school/park sites and other arterial infrastructure underway, with significant quantities of undeveloped land within these areas still to be developed without any timeline for the funding and construction of additional schools long overdue; 4. The underlying desire to also develop urban developable land inside the Urban Containment Boundary within Fernridge, Booth and Rinn Neighbourhood Plans remains strong; and 5. Residents have consistently requested a more responsible growth plan to include greater consideration of new schools, urban parks, tree canopy retention, roads, sidewalks, active transportation, recreation facilities and other amenities and local services; Therefore be it resolved that Council requests a report to Council to amend the Willoughby Development Phasing Council Policy 07-237 and confirm the intent to: 1) Update the numbering scheme for Section 4.1 to be 4.1.1, 4.1.2, 4.1.3 and 4.1.4; 2) Add a new 4.1.3(b) specific to the Latimer Neighbourhood Plan that includes the land area contained within the Detention Pond 6 catchment area roughly bounded by 200 Street to 205 Street and 73 Avenue to 76 Avenue; 3) Add a new 4.1.3(c) specific to the Northeast Gordon Estate Neighbourhood Plan that includes the land area contained within the Detention Pond 9 catchment area roughly bounded by 207 Street to 208 Street and 68 Avenue to 72 Avenue; and 4) Add a new 4.1.3(d) specific to the Smith Neighbourhood Plan that includes the land area contained within the Detention Pond 6 catchment area roughly bounded by 204 Street to 208 Street and 72 Avenue to 74 Avenue.

Title: Micromobility Pilot Program
Motion text: Whereas: 1. Research from the University of British Columbia and data obtained through the first phase of the Province of British Columbia’s Electric Kick Scooter Pilot Project has shown that trips made by micromobility devices, like electric bikes (e-bikes) and electric kick scooters (e-kick scooters), can frequently replace vehicle trips thus contributing to reduced road congestion. 2. Data from municipalities within Metro Vancouver that have launched shared micromobility programs since 2021 have seen significant ridership with few reported injuries or serious safety incidents. 3. New mobility options like shared micromobility can provide safe and accessible transportation for a variety of ages and abilities and can function as a helpful “last mile” connection to transit. 4. Shared micromobility operators use GPS tools to track devices enabling them to control speed, riding locations (i.e., restrict areas like sidewalks), and device pick-up/drop-off areas increasing user and community safety. Therefore be it resolved that Council hereby directs staff to prepare a Memo to Council which includes an update on the four-year extension of the O. OTHER BUSINESS Province’s Electric Kick Scooter Pilot Project and any associated implications for the Township.

Title: Enforcement of Agricultural Land Commission Decisions
Motion text: Whereas: The Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) is the administrative tribunal that adjudicates applications in the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR), the provincial zone in British Columbia that preserves agricultural land; The ALC ultimately determines the usage of the ALR land, taking precedence over other legislation and bylaws applying to the land; The responsibility for ALC decisions, including rectifying violations and enforcing decisions, often falls to municipal governments, regardless of whether the municipality supports the decision, which transfers provincial responsibilities and costs down to local government: Therefore be it resolved that staff forward this Council resolution to the Union of British Columbia Municipalities (UBCM) requesting that UBCM lobby the Government of British Columbia to assume responsibility for the enforcement of Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) decisions and any municipal costs incurred as a result of ALC decisions.

Title: Additional Principles for Booth, Rinn and Fernridge 3.0
Motion text: Whereas: 1. On January 29, 2024, Council endorsed a further revision to the Booth, Rinn and Fernridge Neighbourhood Plans due to the requirement for the provision of small-scale multi-unit buildings on any single family lot greater than 280 m2, based on Report to Council 24-17, and the dramatic increases in unanticipated projected residential densities without a proper planning and public process this has caused; 2. The Township of Langley has a long-standing goal within the Official Community Plan to see one local job for every working resident, of which they should be as high-quality as possible; and 3. Council has received significant feedback on environmental, educational, recreational and greenway objectives that could potentially be further considered within an additional revisionary planning process. Therefore be it resolved that Council endorses the following additional principles for the upcoming, subsequent Booth, Rinn, and Fernridge Neighbourhood Plans revisions, as it may be appropriate for the public’s and Council’s consideration: A. Additional environmental preservation and pervious area setbacks in additional to minimum SPEA requirements for Little Campbell River and/or other important waterways, subject to the removal of previously lower- density housing forms with lower percentages of impervious services that local government no longer controls and can no longer ensure; B. Exploration of employment land options, including area(s) located adjacent to Campbell Heights; C. The potential establishment of Special Study Areas and/or other mechanisms for subarea(s) for which residential development of the forms still controlled by local government are potentially inappropriate to designate; D. The potential expansion of trail connections between Campbell Valley Regional Park and the developed areas of Brookswood, including, but not necessarily limited to, the Derek Doubleday Arboretum, if possible; P. OTHER BUSINESS [name removed] preservation or park space(s) within the lands known as “Horne Pit”; and F. Ensuring quality urban planning for upcoming urban areas in South Langley that generally maintains projected, reasonable and established residential densities despite the inability to now create lower density residential single family subdivisions with certainty; and G. Options to streamline and improve the flexibility and responsiveness of the neighbourhood planning process and subsequent governing documents.

Title: Additional Truck Parking in the Township of Langley
Motion text: Whereas: 1. Trucks and efficient transport play a critical role in the national and local economy, ensuring the timely transportation and movement of goods throughout the region; 2. There is a significant regional shortage of industrial lands, including purpose-built truck parking, creating economic and everyday operations challenges for truckers leading to the proliferation of truck parking on agricultural and rural lands with the Agriculture Land Reserve; and 3. The Township of Langley Council wants to find solutions to address the issue of truck parking, while ensuring environmental protection and preserving rural lands, character and agricultural land for its intended purpose. Therefore be it resolved that Council hereby directs staff to report to Council on: (1) options to increase the quantity of truck parking on urban, non-ALR lands, including within new or existing employment lands areas; (2) potential Township of Langley land that could serve as short-term truck parking facilities; and (3) review of the City of Surrey’s Truck Parking Strategy with recommendations that may or may not be applicable within the Township of Langley; and further That Mayor and Council write to: (1) the Minister of Agriculture to outline that it does not support changes to the Agricultural Land Commission or Agricultural Land Reserve Acts that would enable the unfettered expansion of industrial truck parks on agricultural lands; and (2) the Minister of Transportation and OTHER BUSINESS Q. https://youtu.be/FZf66hVXDXE?t=9419 Infrastructure to request a regional solution to truck parking and that the industry problem can no longer be ignored.

Implement a triannual meter reading and billing schedule in 2025 and transition to quarterly billing complete with associated resource requirements by 2027. 6. Prepare a comprehensive public communications and engagement strategy. 7. Title: Business Licence Reform for Township of Langley Businesses
Motion text: Be it resolved that Council hereby directs staff to report to Council with draft bylaw amendments to Licensing Bylaw 2016 No 5192, as amended, as may be appropriate for Council to consider, to: A. Differentiate between simple and complex licence types as the potential basis for a revised policy framework to streamline the business licence processes, application requirements and renewal timelines for a majority of Township of Langley businesses; B. Create options for up to 5, 10 and other multi-year business licences for simple commercial, office, and industrial categories that are not home- based, with additional provisions to revoke Business Licences, if necessary; C. Consider applicable cost savings for multi-year new licences and renewals, potentially partially offset with adjustments to other complex categories that have other requirements and additional processing overhead; D. Consolidate, reduce and/or remove Business Licence categories as it may be practical, possible and applicable; E. Consolidate and rescind Council Policies 07-406 Licensing, 07-407 Liquor Licensing and 07-411 Renewal of Existing Licenses Enforcement into Licensing Bylaw 2016, 5192, as amended; F. Reduce requirements within Section 4.1(2)(b) for Business Premises where information from previous applicants, licences and/or construction permits is available, potentially with representations made that a Business Premises has remained unchanged; G. Improve or remove Sections 4.3(1) and for the Township of Langley to allow some or all simple Licence types to secure private insurance as they determine is required, subject to legal review; H. Otherwise reduce and/or remove requirements and processes that involve the Township of Langley enforcing Applicable Laws of other levels of government where there is no direct responsibility of, or identified need for, or benefit to the Township of Langley to do so, or for this enforcement to apply to a limited subset of applicable Business Licence categories; and P. OTHER BUSINESS I. Present Council with any other improvements to streamline, improve and reduce application overhead for Township of Langley businesses and staff to complete Business Licensing at a reduced cost, reduced timelines and over inconvenience to Township of Langley businesses.

Title: Mayor’s Task Force on the Langley Regional Airport Recommended Motion
Motion text: That Council direct staff to Report to Council with a comprehensive review of options and recommendations for the future of the Langley Regional Airport; That a Report to Council include a potential approach for developing a long- term Strategic Plan for the Langley Regional Airport 2045 that would include, but not necessarily limited to: • a long-term vision for the facility; • identified priorities for the Airport's development and operation; • an action plan and timeline for necessary objectives; • a 15-year capital plan; and • extensive and ongoing consultation with affected airport lease holders, users, tenants and the public; That a Report to Council include a review of all operating costs to identify potential opportunities for cost reductions directed to the Airport Reserve; That a Report to Council outline an Airport Maintenance Charge that could be applied to all leaseholders for the purpose of capital revenues for future capital projects, for Council to consider; That a Report to Council identify potential funding sources for critical capital projects that are required in the immediate and medium term; That a Report to Council identify potential governance models for the Langley Regional Airport, including but not necessarily limited to, the Airport Authority model, the municipal corporation model, local government society model, commission model and the existing in-house Township model, with recommendations for Council to consider; P. Title: RCMP Contract Budget Implications for 2025 and 2026
Note: Vote on the main Motion.
Motion text: Whereas: 1. Within the 2023 Budget and 2023-2027 Five Year Financial Plan, for 2023, RCMP contract cost increases were an additional $2.5M per year to the base budget, representing a 1.6% property tax increase; 2. Within the 2024 Budget and 2024-2028 Five Year Financial Plan, for 2024, RCMP cost increases were an additional $4.6M per year to the base budget, representing a 2.8% property tax increase; 3. Within the 2025 Budget and 2025-2029 Five Year Financial Plan, for 2025, RCMP costs are potentially up to an additional $5.5M+ per year to the base budget approximately, indefinitely, representing a potential additional property tax increase of 3.1%, possibly more, due, in part, to the transition to the Surrey Police Service within the City of Surrey; 4. Over three years, this represents a budgetary increase of approximately $12.5M+ and possibly as much as a 7.5% property tax increases confirmed and downloaded to the Township of Langley (and other local governments) by other levels of government; 5. The mandated transition within the City of Surrey to the Surrey Police Service by the BC NDP could have significant financial implications on administrative and regional costs for remaining RCMP municipalities within Metro Vancouver and/or British Columbia; 6. In 2022, the overall average cost per RCMP member per annum was approximately $190,000, and in 2025 may be as high as $242,000 per member per annum; and 7. These per year increases represent a significant financial challenge for the Township of Langley taxpayers in a time of rising cost of living pressures, where, to absorb these increases other desirable outcomes, service level improvements and capital objectives may need to be deferred; OTHER BUSINESS [name removed] be it resolved that Council hereby directs staff to report to Council, before the end of Q3 2024, confirming and outlining for Council’s consideration the additional costs for RCMP services for the 2025-2029 five year financial plan, with sources of cost increases and long-term requirements, with any applicable recommendations that may be appropriate for Council to consider.

Title: Provincial and Regional Property Tax Statement Separation
Motion text: Whereas: 1. Provincial and regional property taxation authorities — BC Assessment, Metro Vancouver, Municipal Finance Authority, Translink and the Ministry of Education — comprise a significant portion of the total applicable property taxes collected by the Township of Langley on their behalf; and 2. There can be significant confusion amongst property taxpayers that the Township of Langley is not responsible for these amounts and the often significant annual increases levied by other entities and the Province of British Columbia; Therefore be it resolved that Council directs staff to report to Council regarding the separation of the regional and provincial property taxing authorities onto a separate property tax statement and invoice beginning within the 2025 taxation year. That this contemplated second property tax statement and invoice clearly indicate: (1) the responsibility of the respective regional and provincial property taxing authorities for the amounts required be paid therein; and (2) that the Township of Langley is the property taxation collection agency only, with no responsibility for nor control over the property taxation amounts that applicable external authorities have chosen to levy. That staff review the additional, potential line item categories that an exclusive Township of Langley property tax statement could and shall include, beginning within the 2025 taxation year, and further That these changes in policy, if so endorsed by Council, be added to Council Policy 03-842 Budget Directives or outlined within a new Property Tax P. Title: Single Stair Egress Revision to the BC Building Code
Motion text: Whereas: 1. The Province of BC has updated the BC Building Code (BCBC) to remove the code requirement for a second egress exit stairway in buildings up to six storeys in height; 2. Two stairways within multi-family apartment buildings supports faster evacuation, provides for an additional egress option if one is compromised, and enables a greater range of emergency response and firefighting strategies; 3. The British Columbia Professional Fire Fighters’ Association and the Greater Vancouver Fire Chiefs’ Association have expressed concerns with the impacts of this decision on firefighting, firefighter safety and impacts on public safety, and with the process used by the Ministry of Housing and the Province of BC to bypass the established national code development and amendment process. Therefore be it resolved that Council endorses a letter to be sent to the BC Minister of Housing requesting that the implementation of the changes to the BC Building Code to allow for single degrees stairways within multi-unit apartment buildings be paused and deferred until safety considerations can P. OTHER BUSINESS be reviewed, and proper consultation with the Fire Chiefs Association of BC and the BC Professional Fire Fighters can be completed, and further That the letter include a request that the Province of British Columbia recommit to following standard national and local building code amendment processes respecting the safeguards provided by that process.

Title: Debt Workshop in 2025 Budget Process
Motion text: Whereas both long-term and “temporary” borrowing by the current Council continues to accumulate and escalate every month; Therefore be it resolved that Council request staff to hold a separate dedicated Council Workshop on the topic of current and projected debt levels in the Township of Langley as part of the 2025 Budget process. Be it further resolved that this Council Workshop on debt include, but not be limited to: 1. Debt levels at the start of this current Council term; 2. New debt totals approved to date in the current Council term; 3. Expected total $ debt from all sources by the end of this current Council’s term; 4. Current annual and anticipated total carrying/debt servicing costs of all the new debt by source and type including, but not limited to, internal borrowing; 5. Debt repayment plans and financing terms for the new debt; 6. Estimated revenue sources from all sources including, but not limited to, property tax increases in both the long and short term to repay the total new debt principal and total annual servicing costs of the new debt; and 7. The Township of Langley’s current 2024 Maximum Debt Ceiling, and the Township’s current 2024 position relative to that Maximum Debt Ceiling. Q. Title: Langley Airport Zoning Regulation Amendment
Note: Vote on the main Motion, as amended. The text shown is the motion as first moved; it was amended before this vote. See the minutes for the final wording.
Motion text: Whereas: 1. The Langley Airport Zoning Regulation (AZR) is mandated by the federal Aeronautics Act and enforced by Transport Canada; 2. To theoretically ensure safe and unobstructed aircraft operations, the AZR limits the maximum height of any building or structure to 53.95 metres geodetic on all properties within a 4 kilometre radius of the Langley Regional Airport; 3. The AZR impacts most of the Willowbrook Community Plan, particularly around the planned Willowbrook SkyTrain Station at Willowbrook Drive and Fraser Highway; and 4. The in-service date for the Surrey-Langley SkyTrain extension has been delayed from 2028 to 2030, and Bus Rapid Transit on 200 Street from Willowbrook to Haney remains unfunded with an unknown timeline; Q. OTHER BUSINESS Therefore be it resolved that Council directs staff to: 1) commence a process to seek an amendment and/or exemption for a portion of the Langley Airport Zoning Regulation (the “AZR”) within the Township of Langley currently in effect for the Willowbrook Community Plan area; 2) engage an aerodrome expert to prepare a summary report for the purposes of an amendment and/or exemption application to the AZR, with a maximum of $150,000 pre-approved within the 2025 Budget; 3) ensure that an aerodrome report is consistent with the future vision and development of the new Langley Regional Airport Strategic Plan that is currently underway; 4) engage with relevant government agencies such as Transport Canada, Nav Canada, BC Ministry of Transportation and Infrastructure and TransLink; and further 5) defer a new Willowbrook Community Plan until the aerodrome report is completed and submitted to Transport Canada for consideration of a Township of Langley AZR amendment and/or exemption.

Title: Additional Waitlist Options for Beginner Swimming Lessons
Motion text: Whereas: 1. In Summer and Fall registration of 2024, for beginner swimming lessons, many thousands of residents were waitlisted for access to swim lessons; 2. Duplicate registrations for multiple classes prevents access for other residents seeking registration and consumes recreational staff resources to manually update; and 3. Many residents remain unable to pre-register for specific days and times that would best suit their schedules and availably, requiring availability for priority access registration at a specific date and time; Therefore be it resolved that Council directs staff to report to Council with additional options for longer-term waitlist and registration options beyond a single season that: 1. considers priority access for the next season of swim lesson registration for verified residents who are waitlisted and did not obtain a swim lesson registration from the prior season; 2. explores additional opportunities to increase lesson capacity where feasible, prioritizing minimal impact on public swim sessions and facility rentals; 3. allows for verified Township of Langley residents to pre-register multiple seasons and/or years (as may be possible) in advance for beginner swim lessons Levels 1-3, and Swimmer 1-3, and other high demand recreational programming that it may be appropriate for Council to consider; and 4. implements measures to minimize duplicate class registrations to maximize availability for a greater number of residents with reduced staff time; and further That staff draft a new Council Policy for previous and current Council direction for swimming lessons and other high demand recreational programming, potentially consolidated with Council Policy 06-006, for Council’s future consideration.

Title: Potential Parking Requirement Reductions for Rapid Transit

Title: Request for a Provincial Municipal Audit and Governance Review
Motion text: Whereas: 1. The present Langley Township Council, in its first 2 years of office alone, has significantly expanded the number and total dollar amount of its Municipal Borrowing Bylaws by $499 Million and total TOL Municipal Debt now stands at $688 Million; 2. The present Langley Township Council has also significantly expanded the number and total dollar amount of its Temporary Borrowing Bylaws in the past year, including a doubling of the 2025 Revenue Anticipation Borrowing Bylaw to $50 Million; 3. On 4 November 2024, the present Langley Township Council rescinded its Budget Directives Policy #03-824 and referred it to staff for “improvements to achieve staff time reductions and process refinements that may be appropriate for Council to consider for the upcoming 2025 and 2026 Five Year Financial Plans” but Council has not yet been provided with any policy replacements to consider although it is now nearly the end of January 2025; 4. As of 11:30am on Wednesday January 22, 2025, which is the time that this Notice of Motion was submitted per the deadlines specified in the Township of Langley Council Procedure Bylaw, Council had not had a 2025 Budget Workshop nor received a Draft 2025 Budget and 5-Year Financial Plan despite repeated requests from various Council members for complete Budget 2025 information; 5. The Mayor of the Township of Langley publicly announced on Thursday January 23, 2025 at the Langley Chamber of Commerce Local Government Reception at 7:36pm that the 2025 TOL Property Tax Increase would be 3.5% + 0.9% for Infrastructure yet Township Council as a whole had not seen, discussed, or even voted on this; and 6. As a consequence, the current Langley Township Council does not have: i) a replacement for the abovementioned rescinded Budget O. OTHER BUSINESS Policy, ii) a 2025 Budget Workshop in any form; iii) a publicly discussed or Council resolution-endorsed draft 2025 Township of Langley (TOL) Budget and 5 Year Financial Plan by January 22, 2025; and iv) all individual Council members have not been afforded the full, fair, and equal opportunity to exercise their complete and proper financial fiduciary due diligence under provincial law especially as the proposed 2025 TOL Budget appeared on the January 27, 2025 Council Agenda at 2:31 pm on January 23. 2025 for resolution/disposition five days later on January 27, 2025. Therefore Be It Resolved that a request be made to the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing to audit and review the compliance of the Township of Langley in its 2024 and 2025 Budget and Reporting Cycles with provincial legislative and policy requirements as well as adherence to Canadian public sector accounting standards; and Be it further resolved that the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing be requested to direct the Inspector of Municipalities under the Local Government Act to facilitate and oversee the aforesaid audit and review.

Title: Township of Langley Parks Master Plan
Topics: Housing & density; Development; Parks & recreation; Governance & elections
Motion text: Whereas: 1. The Township of Langley has one of the highest growth rates in Metro Vancouver with significant increases in housing supply projected within the Willoughby and Willowbrook areas to 2040, with urban land values continually increasing, especially within proximity to Rapid Transit due to the negative impacts of “Bill 47”; 2. Council has not adopted nor considered the formal adoption of a new Parks and Recreation Master Plan since the adoption of the 2002 Parks and Recreation Master Plan adopted by Council on July 15, 2002; 3. A number of new recreation facilities have been constructed over that time, such as the Langley Events Centre, the Aldergrove Community Centre, Yorkson Community Park and salishan Place, with Ice Sheet and Dry Floors and Smith Athletic Park now under construction, without an overall master plan that outlined these facilities, specifically, suggesting that a Parks Master Plan could be considered as a distinct plan unto itself; 4. As outlined within the Township of Langley 2002 Parks and Recreation Master Plan, the standard of supply for parks includes a total of four (4) acres of Municipal Park, two (2) acres of Neighbourhood Park and two (2) acres of Community Park, each per 1,000 residents, given that quality park and nature spaces provide numerous benefits for physical and mental health; P. OTHER BUSINESS 5. Due to increased density and housing mandates, the Township of Langley is potentially facing a significant deficit in natural spaces in or within close proximity to developing urban areas, especially within 200 Street 2040 and other ongoing housing supply increases per acre for areas that remain undeveloped; 6. The Willoughby and Willowbrook areas are projected to be more dense than other areas of the Township of Langley, while not within as close a proximity to a Regional Park, such as Campbell Valley; and 7. Outlining and adopting a potential Parks Master Plan for residents and future Councils would have the benefit of potentially enabling the creation of a new Municipal Park in Willoughby that would require the commitment of multiple Councils to complete; Therefore be it resolved that staff present to Council on the merits, or lack thereof, of creating and adopting a Parks Master Plan 2025-2040 with a scope that potentially includes, but is not necessarily limited to: 1. An inventory of the needed Neighbourhood and Community Parks within urban and developing areas, as projected; 2. Additional athletic amenities that may be required within urban and developing areas; 3. A new Nathan Creek Municipal Park in Glen Valley; 4. A new passive park within Aldergrove Urban Containment Boundary; 5. A new passive park adjacent to the Smith Neighbourhood Plan; and 6. A new, extensive, signature Municipal Park in Willoughby, potentially connecting 202A and 208 Streets.

Title: Urban Schools for 200 Street and Within Willowbrook
Motion text: Whereas: 1. The Coal Harbour elementary school, childcare facility, and social housing project in the City of Vancouver provides a good regional example of the potential for new elementary schools to be integrated into mixed-use housing developments; Therefore be it resolved that Council directs staff to present to Council on potential urban schools to be considered as part of the Willoughby and Willowbrook Community Plan updates, and to confirm with School District 35 its willingness, or lack thereof, to consider urban schools within the 200 Street Corridor and Willowbrook Community Plan area given the economics of development and Provincial housing mandates.

Title: Suspension of Joint School Park Sites Land Acquisitions
Note: Vote on the main Motion.
Motion text: Whereas: Report to Council 23-260, dated December 4, 2023, outlines and quantifies that the Township of Langley is facing an increasing land acquisition liability of at least $525M in 2023 dollars to subsidize Provincial acquisition and construction of new schools, a reported minimum of $276M in Willoughby and $259M in Brookswood/Fernridge; P. OTHER BUSINESS These financial projections do not account for inflationary pressure on urban land values to 2050, additional middle school sites being requested by School District 35, population increases with higher density development, nor any additional subsidy due to housing Provincial housing mandates due to “Bill 44” and “Bill 47”; and The current community planning and policy contexts for Willoughby do not include nor contemplate the provision of a new, needed Township Municipal Park for natural and conservation purposes within these densifying areas; Therefore be it resolved that Council endorse the suspension of the Township’s current and future joint park-school site land acquisition program, in principle, effective immediately, and directs staff to report to Council with, but not necessary limited to: 1. An updated land cost projections for Willoughby and Brookswood/Fernridge Neighbourhood and Community Parks, unadjusted, within a potential update to the Development Cost Charge Program therefrom starting in 2026, assuming inflationary pressures as accurately as can be predicted; 2. An additional, further financial review of the long-term opportunity cost implications adversely affecting the Township of Langley’s ability to provide Municipal Natural Park spaces within its developing areas of Willoughby, in addition to playing fields or athletic facilities at Neighbourhood and Community Parks for school sites and ongoing subsidization of School District 35 and the Province of British Columbia; 3. An additional, further review to determine the necessity of a suspension to the school park site acquisition program to ensure that a signature Municipal Park natural park of significant scale can be contemplated within Willoughby for a more livable and balanced community in the Township of Langley’s higher density areas; and 4. A review of all existing and planned Elementary, Middle, and Secondary School locations in Willoughby, with a goal of ensuring the School District is maintaining onsite parking requirements as required by bylaw or the Township of Langley’s site specific development requirements, and an overview of each site’s current use of the playground and student exterior play spaces that were constructed, and the need for potential Council Policy updates therefrom. That staff present to Council on the merits, or lack thereof, of a potential new Council Policy context whereby the ownership of currently undeveloped sites, and future land acquisitions for the purposes of new schools, reverts to being the sole responsibility of School District 35, the Ministry of Education and Child Care, and/or the Ministry of Infrastructure as it appears to be within every other municipality within the Province of British Columbia, while the Township of Langley could consider to continue providing park and P. OTHER BUSINESS playing field development, booking services, and ongoing maintenance at the sites within a mutually acceptable land lease arrangement. That Council Policies 06-023 and 07-229 be rescinded, and Section 4.9 of Council Policy 07-231 be removed with subsequent items renumbered. That School District 35 and the Ministry of Education and/or Ministry of Infrastructure be informed that the Township of Langley owned land adjacent to a future West Latimer Elementary School designated for the purposes of constructing an elementary school is available to School District 35 for its acquisition with the park-school site land acquisition program hereby suspended, to instead be potentially developed, operated and maintained within a new, updated Council Policy context, if so adopted by Council. DEFERRAL

Title: Updated Fees and Charges for Aquatic and Recreation Facilities
Motion text: Whereas: 1. The annual net operating subsidy from property taxes for WC Blair Recreation Centre is estimated to be $2.1M, Walnut Grove Community Centre $2.3M, and the Aldergrove Community Centre $3.4M, totalling $7.8M per annum; P. OTHER BUSINESS 2. The annual net operating subsidy from property taxes for George Preston Recreation Centre is estimated to be $2.5M per annum; 3. The annual net operating subsidy from property taxes for McLeod Athletic Park is estimated to be $731K per annum, the athletic park provided by the Township of Langley for Langley Senior Secondary School, where student enrolment is 60% from the City of Langley; 4. The annual net operating subsidies from property taxes of Smith Athletic Park and the Ice Sheets and Dry Floor Arenas at the Langley Events Centre is yet to be determined, but will add to the net annual net operating subsidies required overall for these world class recreational facilities; and 5. The significant, subsidized operating and ongoing capital renewal cost of these facilities for Greater Langley as borne by property taxpayers falls solely to Township of Langley residents and businesses, and continues to increase annually with inflation and other cost pressures, a situation that has persisted for many years without resolution; Therefore be it resolved that Council directs staff to report to Council, with a timeline for implementation as soon as practically possible, on: 1. The implementation of an external surcharge or Township of Langley resident discount within the Fees and Charges Bylaw 4616 specific to recreation facilities with aquatics to assist with the significant net operating subsidies required from Township of Langley property taxpayers to provide these facilities to the Greater Langley population; and 2. Priority access registration for Township of Langley residents currently in place for swim lessons be extended to other high demand recreational programming, as it may be appropriate for Council to consider, including during the summer season at the Aldergrove Community Centre. Further, that Council directs staff to review potential revised operating models in partnership with primary user groups for McLeod Athletic Park, Willoughby Community Park and the upcoming Smith Athletic Park and Ice Sheet and Dry Floor Arenas at the Langley Events Centre to help offset the net annual operating subsidies required for these current and future facilities for the Greater Langley population.

Title: Potential Partnerships for Dredging of the Bedford Channel
Note: Vote on the main Motion, as amended. The text shown is the motion as first moved; it was amended before this vote. See the minutes for the final wording.
Motion text: Whereas: 1. Staff provided Council an update to Bedford Channel Dredging Project Updated dated February 24, 2025, 5260-21-015-01, outlining that the process for completing an application to other levels of government is well underway and ongoing; 2. Dredging of the Fraser River has typically been a Provincial, Federal and/or Port of Vancouver responsibility, while the Bedford Channel has unique benefits to the local community and region in terms of accessibility for rowing and canoeing user groups and other recreational purposes; and 3. The Kwantlen First Nation and local user groups of the Bedford Channel have expressed a desire for dredging of the Bedford Channel to proceed as soon as possible, and to retain any dredged material for future projects and ongoing flood mitigation efforts; Therefore be it resolved that Council directs staff to: 1. confirm a more accurate projection of potential project costs, assuming local retention of material in partnership with the Kwantlen First Nation; 2. identify potential funding sources from community partners, Metro Vancouver and/or grants from other levels of government that may be possible to confirm and coordinate a cost-sharing partnership with the Kwantlen First Nation and the Township of Langley; 3. complete a plan for dredging as it may be possible within 2025/2026 given Water Sustainability Act (and other) permitting requirements still awaiting completion of any required environmental and species impacts assessment(s) as may be required by other levels of government; and 4. consideration of, as may be possible, an ongoing Bedford Channel maintain and dredging plan, in partnership with the Kwantlen First Nation, for the Bedford Channel to be dredged on a more regular basis. P. OTHER BUSINESS

Title: Fraser Highway Employment Lands Reference Plan
Motion text: Whereas: 1. The Township of Langley has now held two public open houses regarding the Fraser Highway Employment Lands Area Plan, October 23, 2024 and January 30, 2025; 2. A range of concerns have been identified with the current process, boundary and the need for more specific designations of current and protected land uses; 3. The current process contemplates only low impact industrial and employment lands within an area and plan boundaries confirmed by Council, where subsequent direction is required for adjustments; and 4. The general benefit for a completed urban planning policy context process and land use planning with safeguards for environmental issues, drainage and services remains; Therefore be it resolved that Council directs staff to complete a draft Reference Plan for the Fraser Highway Employment Lands Area Plan for its consideration, subject to the following adjustments: 1. That future access through redevelopment for properties with frontages on both Fraser Highway and Old Yale Road be limited to Fraser Highway only; 2. That blanket industrial lands designations be updated to reflect and retain the existing mobile home park, residential, commercial, and mixed-use designations and land uses along with proposed institutional and employment lands designations, as appropriate for Council to consider, P. OTHER BUSINESS with expanded clarity that only low impact employment lands uses are to be considered where so designated; and 3. That the proposed boundary within Concept Plan Option 1 and 2 be reduced, as it may be appropriate for Council to consider, to remove lands: (a) east of 232 Street and in direct proximity to 46 Avenue; (b) fronting Old Yale Road without access to Fraser Highway or 232 Street north of 4104-232 Street; and (c) north of 44 Avenue and east of 23433 - 44 Avenue. That Council directs staff to include the following components in the draft Reference Plan: (a) specific land use policies; (b) public realm, parks and open space policies; (c) mobility policies such as location for collectors, trails and multi-use pathways; (d) design guidelines for various Development Permits Areas, such as form and character of development, Agricultural Land Reserve and urban edge planning buffers, and environmental setbacks for Streamside Protection and Enhancement Areas; and (e) an Engineering Servicing Plan. That Council directs staff to conduct a 3rd public open house on the Fraser Highway Employment Lands Area Plan to present a revised Option 4 and obtain community feedback. That Council endorses the completion of a Reference Plan, if so endorsed by Council, as a framework for evaluating development applications within the ultimate planning area and individual applications for amendments to the Metro Vancouver Regional Growth Strategy, if approved in principle by Council. That Council directs staff to conduct public consultation on a proposed concept for the closure of Old Yale Road at approximately the 23900 block, along with a proposed ultimate design for 240 Street and Fraser Highway. That staff Present to Council on its legal and practical options regarding the current operation, potential expansion and/or beneficial relocation of the Vancouver Ready Mix at 22765 Fraser Highway, given that is an existing legal non-conforming use within the Urban Containment Boundary.

Title: Potentially Reducing Barriers for Urban Trail Users
Motion text: Whereas the Township of Langley’s Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw includes Section L4 – ‘Trails’, which details the design standards that all Urban and Rural trails are built to, Whereas Section L4.4 – ‘Restrictive Barriers’ details the types of barriers that are used where trails intersect with driveways and intersecting roads, which includes a “bicycle stop baffle” at the entrance of trails, Whereas these bicycle stop baffles are designed to reduce negative interactions between cyclists and pedestrians, but limit the ability for various users, such as those with cargo bikes and bikes with passenger trailers, in using the Township’s expanding trail network, and Whereas there are potentially other barrier types that can be used to slow cyclists and prevent access to automobiles while still facilitating the safe use of trails by all users, Therefore be it resolved that Council be updated by staff on work being undertaken to identify potential changes to the Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw that may eliminate the use of bicycle stop baffles on the Township of Langley’s Urban Trail network in favour of other, more accessible trail barriers, and Be it further resolved that staff include in the update to Council a list of locations of current bicycle stop baffles in areas of key importance to the Township’s urban cycling network, and that this list include potential costs associated with the replacement of the bicycle stop baffles with more accessible trail barriers.

Title: Potential Rural Sign Bylaw Reform
Motion text: Whereas the Township of Langley Sign Bylaw 2012 No. 4927 includes Part 4 - Signs Permitted in Rural Areas, P. OTHER BUSINESS Whereas the fair application of Part 4 depends on the interpretation of staff and Rural Community which can, on occasion, differ, and Whereas this difference in interpretation causes added complexity and causes unnecessary work for both staff and those in the Rural Community who are attempting to advertise their farm-based businesses, Therefore be it resolved that Council request staff to consult with the Agriculture Advisory Committee on potential changes to Part 4 of Township of Langley Sign Bylaw 2012 No. 4927 with the goal of simplifying the language and reducing opportunities for confusion, and Be it further resolved that staff report back to Council with the potential changes alongside possible opportunities for public engagement and further refinements.

Title: Rural and Local Road Reconstruction Program, 2026-2028
Motion text: WHEREAS: 1. The Township of Langley has an urban and rural local road inventory of 470km, many of which are contained within rural areas from Glen Valley to High Point; 2. As of 2020, a significant inventory of the Township of Langley’s urban and local roads — 175km — are in poor or very poor condition, facing a chronic state of disrepair where repeatedly attempting interim repairs is no longer cost effective nor practical to continue as is, where rehabilitation of full reconstruction is ultimately required; and 3. Local road rehabilitation and paving has been chronically underfunded for many years leading to the current situation requiring a significant catch up and rehabilitation of roads in poor or very poor condition, both necessary and financially prudent; O. OTHER BUSINESS Therefore be it resolved that Council directs staff to Report to Council no later than October 20th, 2025, with a potential urban and rural local road rehabilitation program for the years 2026-2028, and 2026-2035, or as it may be otherwise appropriate to propose for its consideration, to be considered by Council for pre-approval and/or inclusion within the 2026-2030 Five Year Financial Plan.

Title: 2025 Utility Billing
Motion text: Whereas there is significant confusion and concern regarding the 2025 Utility Billing; Whereas residents, particularly those living in stratified buildings, have expressed confusion and concern that utility rates are increasing significantly; Whereas the Township is committed to transparency, equity, and clear communication with residents; Now Therefore Be It Resolved That: 1. Staff be directed to review the current utility billing structure for stratified developments and determine the appropriate framework to ensure that all components of stratified properties — including individual residential units, commercial units, and common property — are billed fairly and equitably; 2. Staff report back on whether the Township has the authority to require the installation of water meters — at the Township’s expense — in all commercial and residential strata units, including common property, and whether this could support a more accurate and equitable billing process; 3. Staff also consider and advise whether, as an alternative to metering, it would be appropriate for the Township to bill individual strata lots based on their unit entitlement, as set out in the registered Strata Plan.

Title: Fort Langley Racquet Sports Court Usage
Motion text: P. OTHER BUSINESS Whereas: 1. On June 9, 2025 in the Regular Meeting for Public Hearing (Agenda Item C.1 – Fort Langley Racquet Sports Policies) Langley Township Council passed a motion that “The operating hours and potential usage for the racquet sports courts adjacent to Fort Langley Community Park be consistent with those throughout the Township of Langley”; 2. Signage on the Fort Langley racquet sports courts located on SD #35 property (Langley Fine Arts School) adjacent to Fort Langley Community Park clearly states: “Court Schedule: Courts can be rented year-round. When not booked, courts can be used on a first-come, first-served basis”; 3. Several community stakeholder groups affected by the use of the Fort Langley racquet sports courts located on SD #35 property (Langley Fine Arts School) adjacent to Fort Langley Community Park such as nearby residential homeowners, tennis court users, and pickleball court users have previously expressed to TOL Council, and continue to express, concerns about noise and court access/usage times; Therefore be it resolved that TOL Council ask staff to convene a public meeting/public open house in Fort Langley of all Fort Langley racquet sports court users and interested community members as soon as reasonably possible, including but not limited to neighboring residential property owners, tennis court users, pickleball court users, and SD #35 users, to determine a Fort Langley racquet sports court usage schedule that is acceptable and reasonable for all affected Fort Langley stakeholders; and Be it further resolved that staff bring forward an agreed recommendation on an acceptable court usage schedule from all affected Fort Langley racquet sports court stakeholders to Council for approval no later than September 15, 2025; and Be it finally resolved that the revised Fort Langley racquet sports court schedule as agreed to by the Fort Langley racquet sports court stakeholders, and as approved by Council, be incorporated into the TOL racquet sports court policy, and posted online and via Fort Langley racquet sports court signage as soon as practically possible after Council approval is given.

Title: Joint Housing Project
Topics: Housing & density; Taxes & spending; Public services
Motion text: Whereas the fastest-growing segment of the population in the coming years is seniors; and Whereas this demographic is increasingly vulnerable to homelessness and living in vehicles due to the rapidly rising cost of living; and Whereas there is currently an inadequate supply of designated housing for seniors and other vulnerable populations within the Township of Langley; and Whereas there is a shortage of other types of supportive and affordable housing across the Township; Therefore be it resolved that Council direct staff to engage in discussions with both the federal government and the Province of British Columbia to explore opportunities for funding, partnership, and support for the development of a purpose-built facility to house these vulnerable populations; and Be it further resolved that this proposed project be situated on the designated Township-owned property at Horne Pit, immediately north of Fire Hall No. 5, which is nearing completion at that location; and Be it finally resolved that staff be directed to report back to Council with potential options and strategies for advancing this project, including possible collaborations with senior levels of government.

Title: Veterans Village Project
Motion text: Whereas veterans have bravely served in the Canadian Armed Forces, often at great personal cost to their lives and long-term health; and Whereas many of these veterans experience Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) and other service-related challenges, resulting in difficult living conditions; and Whereas a significant number of veterans are unhoused, living in inadequate or unsafe conditions, and lacking access to necessary support services; and Whereas this vulnerable population continues to grow, along with the need for stable housing and appropriate care; Therefore be it resolved that Council direct staff Report to Council with potential options and potential costs to begin the process for developing a Veterans Village within the Township of Langley, and consult with Homes For Heroes, the Royal Canadian Legion, and any other veterans organization; and Be it further resolved that staff be directed to contact and advocate to both the provincial and federal governments to explore opportunities for partnership, funding, and support to advance this potential project.

Title: Residential Interim Detention Servicing for Williams Neighbourhood Plan
Topics: Housing & density; Development; Environment & climate; Public services
Motion text: Whereas: 1. The Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw restricts the use of interim on-site stormwater detention unless land for a permanent detention facility has been secured; 2. For the northern catchment of the Williams Neighbourhood Plan area, the Township has identified the required land for the permanent detention facility and has executed both a DCC Front-Ending Agreement (DCCFA) and a Development Works Agreement (DWA); and 3. Title: RV Tenant Protection
Topics: Housing & density; Taxes & spending; Business & economy; Governance & elections
Motion text: That the following motion be forwarded to the Lower Mainland Local Government Association for submission in the 2026 Conference resolutions: O. OTHER BUSINESS Whereas: 1. As a result of British Columbia’s worsening cost-of-living crisis, more people are finding the most affordable home in which to reside is a Recreational Vehicle (RV) parked at a RV Park or a Manufactured Home Park, 2. These RVs are technically only permitted to remain on-location for a short period of time, in most cases a maximum of 6-months, and have no permanent structures or fixtures, 3. RV owners are not able to sign tenancy agreements with their landlords, only License to Occupy agreements, which do not afford them the same protections or rights as they would be entitled to under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act, 4. Landlords are taking advantage of the precarious living conditions that these RV owners find themselves in, resulting in arbitrary evictions, drastic rental rate hikes, and other negative consequences for the RV owners, 5. There are jurisdictions across North America that have greater legal protections in place for RV owners who rent space within RV or Manufactured Home Parks, and; 6. Only the Province of British Columbia has the authority to create any legal protection for these RV owners during the ongoing cost-of-living crisis: Therefore be it resolved that the UBCM call on the Government of British Columbia to examine policy changes to provide rental protection to long-term RV-based tenants in RV and Mobile Home Parks across British Columbia.

Title: Reports To Council
Motion text: Action C1.2 - Work to upgrade existing cycling and micromobility routes to align with current design guidelines (Page 61) In support of this action, the Township will: ● Develop an investment a funding program focused on upgrading existing cycling and micromobility routes identified as priorities through community engagement and that do not meet current design guidelines, where feasible. ● Continue to upgrade existing cycling and micromobility routes as part of development projects, road rehabilitation, and standalone upgrade projects, based on the results of the Active Transportation Network Assessment. ● Continue to monitor updates to active transportation design guidelines.

Title: Reports To Council
Motion text: Action C1.4: Provide a network of routes that are comfortable for most users. (Page 62) Comfortable for most routes can consist of physically separated facilities, such as multi-use pathways (also included as part of the pedestrian network) and protected bicycle lanes and cycle tracks on streets with high traffic volumes and/or speeds, as well as neighbourhood bikeways. Neighbourhood bikeways are signed bikeways on low volume neighbourhood streets, where cyclists travel on-street with vehicles. These streets have lower speed limits and traffic volumes, and potential traffic calming features implemented by the Township. Cycling and micromobility networks typically also include routes with less comfortable supporting facilities that provide more options for cyclists but may not be suitable for all. This includes bicycle accessible shoulders and painted bicycle lanes (Figure 12). E. REPORTS TO COUNCIL All references to ‘Cycle Tracks’ should be removed from the Study.

Title: Reports To Council
Motion text: Action W1.4 - Expand and enhance existing greenways and trails, and the on-street connections to them. (Pages 73 & 113) As part of this action, the Township will consider take the following next steps: ● Complete a condition assessment of existing greenways and multi- use paths as a short-term action and identify locations for rehabilitation, where necessary. ● In the short-term, complete a pedestrian facility implementation plan, referenced on Page 104, inclusive of greenways, sidewalks, and other pedestrian facilities with gaps identified during Rounds 1-3 of Engagement on the Transportation and Mobility Strategy and through ongoing community engagement. This plan should rank gaps using criteria such: ○ connectivity to transit, schools, and community hubs; ○ collision and safety data; ○ the number of residents served; ○ and input received through community engagement. ● In the short-term, identify potentially suitable portions of urban greenways and trails where additional lighting could be added to enhance community safety. ● Continue interdepartmental coordination (working with the Township parks and recreation team) to implement recommendations and the proposed greenways identified in Neighbourhood and Community Plans, Services Servicing Plans, the OCP, and the TMS. ● Through the update to the Rural Plan, the Township will continue to explore opportunities to implement multi-use pathways along utility rights-of-way. The Township will also continue to work with the equestrian community to maintain, and explore potential options to expand, equestrian access and designated equestrian routes in more rural areas of the Township. ● Work with Metro Vancouver and other organizations to expand the regional trail network.

Title: Reports To Council
Motion text: E. REPORTS TO COUNCIL Action W2.1 - Create new and enhance existing crossings to accommodate people of all ages and abilities, this includes both operational and infrastructure enhancements. (Pages 75 & 113) ● Explore the feasibility of implementing. Wherever possible, implement new mid-block crossings to ensure there are safe places to cross the street. Additional crossing locations will be explored added where demand warrants, providing more safe and accessible crossings at greenways/trails, in community hubs, and access to parks and schools, and near bus stops throughout the community. Add an additional ‘next step’ on Page 75: ● Identify intersections where curb extensions and/or raised crosswalks are feasible for short-term implementation.

Title: Reports To Council
Motion text: Action D1.4 - Continue to monitor motor vehicle delays and identify opportunities to increase overall people-moving capacity through targeted investments in transit reliability and active transportation. (Page 87) In support of this action, the Township will consider the following next steps. ● Implement a recurring program to monitor motor vehicle delays, travel times, and reliability on key arterial corridors. ● Access roadway capacity using a people-moving lens, identifying corridors where transit or active transportation could carry a greater share of trips. ● Consider undertaking In the short-term, undertake a comprehensive examination of the practical applications for Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) in the Township, which could include the provision of real time information to drivers, dynamic corridor signal coordination, transit signal prioritization, as well as future oriented applications such as vehicle to infrastructure technology. ITS technology is relatively new, it creates a communication link between the various vehicles and road systems including traffic signals, transit vehicles, and all other road users providing drivers (and autonomous vehicles in the future) with advance warning about changing or upcoming travel conditions. ● Identify potential corridors for signal coordination, with transit signal prioritization included at key intersections. ● Coordinate with TransLink and BC Transit to identify and advance targeted transit reliability measures, such as transit signal priority, queue jumps, or curbside bus lanes (Action T2.2). E. REPORTS TO COUNCIL ● Evaluating and implementing active transportation improvements as capacity solutions, particularly in corridors with short to medium- length trips and strong transit connections (Action C1.1). ● Using the monitoring results to inform capital planning and prioritizing investments that improve reliability, increase people- moving capacity, and align with long-term mobility objectives.

Motion text: Whereas: 1. The Milner-Langley area is the birthplace of agriculture in British Columbia. 2. The Township of Langley has the most farms in the Metro Vancouver Regional District. 3.
