Title: Advocacy Letter on the Federal Salmon Allocation Policy
Topics: Environment & climate; Business & economy; Governance & elections
Motion text: Whereas: 1. The BC Wildlife Federation (BCWF) and the BC Drift Fishers Association held a well-attended public Town Hall Meeting at the Murrayville Southridge Church on Saturday April 18, 2026; P. OTHER BUSINESS 2. The purpose of this Townhall Meeting was to provide information and education on the pending changes to the federal 1999 Salmon Allocation Policy, and the federal government’s requirement for public consultation on these pending changes as announced on December 5, 2025; 3. Removal of public fishing as a “Common Law Property” right concerns the public’s future right to fish and how the fisheries in Canada are managed in trust by the Government of Canada for all Canadians; 4. The public’s right to fish and the public’s current small share of fisheries in BC and Canada generates the most economic return, the highest conservation rates of Chinook, Coho, Pink, Sockeye, and Chum salmon as an example; and the introduction of a larger proportion of young people and children to the importance of stream stewardship and fish protection via public fishing (see the BCWF webinar available on fishingrights.ca); and 5. Langley Township for decades has been a supporter of public stewardship and river protection in the Township’s 800+ km of salmon bearing water routes throughout our community as well as several river stewardship groups in Langley such as the Salmon River Enhancement Society. Therefore be it resolved that the Langley Township Council send a strong advocacy letter to the Federal Minister of Fisheries, the Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Fisheries, and all MP’s and MLA’s in Langley Township in support of preserving the importance of river conservation and stewardship, and the common property asset of the public’s right to fish relative to any proposed changes to the existing 1999 Salmon Allocation Policy, as well as the need for continued public management in trust for all Canadians of this crucial natural resource by the Government of Canada.

Title: Single Exit Stairwell Residential Buildings
Motion text: Whereas Council supports a broad range of housing options and recognizes the importance of increasing housing supply within the community; and Whereas Council recognizes that residential developments must align with the public safety resources and emergency response capabilities available within the Township; and Whereas the Province of British Columbia amended the British Columbia Building Code in August 2024 to permit certain residential buildings to be constructed with a single egress stairwell under specified conditions; and Whereas Council wishes to better understand the implications of single-exit stairwell residential developments on public safety, emergency response, and future development within the Township; and Whereas Council remains committed to working collaboratively with applicants and development partners to support safe and compliant housing solutions while maintaining resident and responder safety; Therefore be it resolved that Council direct staff to prepare a policy regarding single-exit stairwell residential buildings for Council's consideration, including an evaluation of: • Fire prevention and inspection capacity; • Fire suppression and emergency response capabilities; • Occupant egress and rescue considerations; • Applicable British Columbia Building Code provisions; • Opportunities for early communication with development applicants regarding the Township's position on single-exit stairwell designs; and • A process for periodic review of the policy to ensure ongoing alignment with available resources, legislation, and regulations. P. OTHER BUSINESS Be it further resolved that staff obtain legal review of the proposed policy, including advice respecting the extent to which the Township may regulate, restrict, or impose requirements related to single-exit stairwell residential developments beyond the minimum requirements established under the British Columbia Building Code and the Building Act.

Title: Rural Drainage Infrastructure Strategy
Motion text: Whereas action items in the Agricultural Viability Strategy, Section 2.2.3, Drainage and Ditch Maintenance, recognize that proper drainage infrastructure is essential to protecting agricultural productivity, preventing flooding and maintaining viable farming operations; and Whereas many agricultural areas throughout the Township continue to experience recurring drainage concerns, flooding events and infrastructure deficiencies; O. OTHER BUSINESS Therefore be it resolved that Council direct staff to report to Council with a Terms of Reference and cost estimate for the development of a prioritized Rural Drainage Improvement Program which includes a comprehensive inventory of the Township's agricultural drainage infrastructure, annual maintenance requirements, ten-year capital plan, estimated costs, and funding opportunities.

Title: Rural Road and Farm Transportation Review
Motion text: Whereas action items in the Agricultural Viability Strategy, Section 2.2.4, Road Access and Traffic issues, recognizes agricultural producers depend on safe and efficient transportation routes for the movement of equipment, livestock and agricultural products; and Whereas increasing traffic volumes and urban development continue to impact rural transportation corridors throughout the Township; Therefore be it resolved that Council direct staff to report to Council with a Terms of Reference and cost estimate for the development of an Agricultural Transportation Study to review key agricultural transportation routes with recommendations to improve farm equipment mobility, intersection safety, bridge capacity and rural road infrastructure.

Title: Green Boulevard & Park Innovation Initiative
Topics: Environment & climate; Parks & recreation; Public services; Business & economy
Motion text: Whereas the Township of Langley is one of British Columbia's premier agricultural communities, with a strong tradition of stewardship of its land, soils, and water; and Whereas parks, boulevards, sports fields, and tree-lined streets deliver meaningful environmental and community benefits, including cooling neighbourhoods, managing stormwater, supporting pollinators, and improving public health; and Whereas municipalities across Canada and abroad are combining drought- tolerant plantings, healthier soils, smart irrigation, rain gardens, and bioswales to reduce water use while keeping public spaces vibrant and functional; Whereas many of these practices are already in place or partially in place within the Township but have not been reviewed together as one integrated program. Therefore Be It Resolved That: Council direct staff to report back on which elements of this Notice of Motion are already reflected in current Township procedures, policies, bylaws, and practices, and to identify additional measures that would support a coordinated Green Boulevard & Park Innovation Initiative, including: 1. Development of a Township-wide Green Infrastructure Strategy for parks, boulevards, medians, trails, and other public open spaces. 2. Identification of locations suited to drought-tolerant grasses, native wildflower and pollinator meadows, rain gardens and bioswales, and expanded tree canopy for urban cooling. 3. Evaluation of water-saving practices, including smart irrigation technology, soil moisture sensors, weather-based controllers, reclaimed water where appropriate, and improved soil specifications and compost amendments to reduce irrigation demand. 4. A review of leading municipal practices from other Canadian and international jurisdictions. 5. Partnership and funding opportunities with local growers, landscape professionals, educational institutions, environmental organizations, and senior levels of government. 6. Recommended pilot demonstration projects to showcase the approaches above. O. OTHER BUSINESS 7. The anticipated environmental, financial, biodiversity, and public health benefits of the initiative.

Title: Targeted Grazing Pilot Program for Wildfire Risk Reduction and Vegetation Management
Motion text: Whereas the Township of Langley owns and maintains parks, greenbelts, road allowances, utility corridors, and natural areas where vegetation contributes to wildfire risk during summer months; and Whereas targeted grazing using sheep and goats has been used successfully across British Columbia and western North America to reduce fine fuels, control invasive vegetation, and lower wildfire risk, while reducing reliance on mowing and herbicides, supporting local agriculture, and lowering greenhouse gas emissions; and Whereas the Township's Operations Centre has already run a limited trial using goats to maintain vegetation at an on-site detention pond and is considering expanding the trial to another Township-owned pond; Therefore Be It Resolved That: Staff be directed to prepare a report on the feasibility of a Targeted Grazing Pilot Program for vegetation management and wildfire fuel reduction on municipally owned lands, including: 1. Identification of suitable Township-owned properties, including parks, greenbelts, hydro corridors, creek corridors, forest interfaces, and road allowances. 2. Anticipated wildfire risk reduction, environmental, and vegetation management benefits. 3. Estimated capital and operating costs, including grazing services, temporary fencing, livestock guardian animals, water supply, transportation, signage, and monitoring. 4. A comparison with current vegetation management practices (mowing, brush cutting, herbicide application, and contracted maintenance) on cost, environmental impact, and operational effectiveness. 5. Partnership opportunities with local farmers, conservation organizations, Indigenous communities where appropriate, and qualified grazing contractors. O. OTHER BUSINESS 6. Grant and funding opportunities from federal, provincial, and regional programs, including those supporting wildfire prevention, FireSmart, climate adaptation, and invasive species management. 7. Recommended size, scope, timeline, and performance measures for a pilot beginning in the 2027 growing season, with the report brought back to Council as part of the 2027 budget and strategic planning process.
